Colab91 — AP Classifier

Sthaan.ai · flagship product

An Electron desktop app that auto-classifies accounts-payable transactions from imported CSVs using a multi-agent LLM pipeline. Raw, inconsistent vendor ledgers go in; clean supplier / spend-category / GL classifications come out — with low-confidence rows flagged for human review. Built end-to-end: ingestion, the four AI agents, a DuckDB data layer, taxonomy and override-rule engines, and the review UI.

The pipeline

CSV ingest→ ① Column Mapping→ ② Research→ ③ Classification→ ④ QC→ Review & Export
1

Column Mapping Agent

Maps arbitrary raw CSV columns onto a canonical schema (supplier_name, spend_amount, gl_code, dates…) so any vendor's export can be ingested without manual setup.

2

Research Agent

Exa-powered web research that enriches each supplier — parent company, industry, NAICS code, products & services, and cited sources — before classification.

3

Classification Agent

Assigns supplier / spend category / GL using the taxonomy plus the researched context, scoped to confirmed suppliers, unclassified rows, or a custom filter.

4

QC Agent

Validates classifications with an algorithmic consolidation pass (L2/L3 spend thresholds) and a gated LLM review pass, flagging low-confidence rows for a human.

① Ingest & Column Mapping

Drop in a raw AP export — here 153,628 rows — and the Column Mapping Agent proposes a canonical mapping that the user can review before import.

② Supplier research & the supplier universe

Suppliers are normalized and de-duplicated into a shared universe (925 here), then the Research Agent enriches each one with web-sourced business context.

③ Classification & ④ QC

Classification runs against the taxonomy with selectable scope; the QC Agent then consolidates and reviews the output.

Taxonomy & review

A configurable L1/L2/L3 taxonomy drives classification, and a pivot view rolls spend up by supplier and category for sign-off.
